after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -7 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -7 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-1 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-7 \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & -7 \\ 4 & 1 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -7 \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 4 & 1 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -7 \\ 0 & 3 & -15 \\ 4 & 1 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -7 \\ 0 & 3 & -15 \\ 0 & 5 & k-28\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 5 & k-28\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & k-3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k-3.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k-3\,⇒\,k=3.
$$

The vectors ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$, ${a}_{3}$, and $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}$ from the decomposition $b={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -9 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$
content.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$

$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+6{x}_{3}=-4 \\ -3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-9 \\ {x}_{3}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 & -4 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 18 & -21 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-18{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+6{x}_{3}=-4 \\ {x}_{2}=-3 \\ {x}_{3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}+6(-1)=-4\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$ and ${a}_{3}:$

$$

$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=2\cdot (-3)\cdot (-1)=6.$

By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$

$$

$$

$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc$, $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨1,7,-6⟩$, $c=⟨-2,-10,12⟩$, and  $u=⟨2,11,-12⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
after.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7 \\ -6\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -10 \\ 12\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 11 \\ -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s-2t=2 \\ 7s-10t=11 \\ -6s+12t=-12\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 7 & -10 & 11 \\ -6 & 12 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & -3 \\ -6 & 12 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}s-2t=2 \\ 4t=-3 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
4t=-3\,⟹\,t=-\frac{3}{4}.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s-2t & =2 \\ s-2(-\frac{3}{4}) & =2 \\ s+\frac{3}{2} & =2 \\ s & =2-\frac{3}{2} \\ s & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=\frac{1}{2},\,t=-\frac{3}{4},$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=\frac{1}{2}b-\frac{3}{4}c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-\frac{3}{4})=-\frac{3}{8}.$
